text:
Lina: Heads-up — console shows p99 jump for /v1/generate on eu-west for the last 30m but per-endpoint p99 doesn't match the single-endpoint query. sample_count also low. Anyone else seeing this?
Raj: yep saw it ~10m ago. Looks like a rollup issue? the UI rollup is mixing route-merge + fallback weights. :thinking:
Sam: can you paste the queries you used? product needs to know if this is real or just a visualization artifact before we alarm customers.
Lina: pasted two quick screenshots (console):
- Rollup view (Route = /v1/generate, timeframe 30m): p50 120ms, p95 420ms, p99 890ms, sample_count: 230
- Endpoint split (by model variant): p99 for variant-a = 210ms, variant-b = 700ms, sample_count sum = 230
But the rollup p99 is 890ms which is > max(variant p99). So it's impossible unless samples outside variants exist.
Eve: maybe some samples are getting tagged with no-variant (fallback path). We had a short period where KV-cache miss path used a different router and omitted the variant tag.
telemetry-bot: Incident note: routing-policy-change deployed at 1735219000 introduced attribute 'route_variant' optional omit.
Raj: That bot note lines up. If missing 'route_variant' then rollup policy could be mixing full-endpoint measurements with model-variant buckets and t-digest merging can produce weird high p99s if there's a tiny high-latency tail in the untagged bucket.
Sam: So this is a provenance/sampling origin problem. Product asks: can we show provenance in the UI or at least annotate rollup percentiles with sample_origin breakdown?
Lina: Proposal: small change in telemetry API: when returning percentiles for a rollup, include metadata: {"sample_origins": ["variant-a: 120", "variant-b: 110", "untagged: 3"]} and a flag if any samples were excluded by the current query filter.
Raj: API change SGTM but two constraints: 1) we must not explode response size for large rollups, and 2) we need to compute counts cheaply (we already compute sample_count though). We could return top-k origins plus an "other_count".
Eve: Implementation detail: in the aggregator, ensure t-digests are only merged across compatible origin tags. If incompatible, we should mark rollup as "mixed-origin" and return an advisory instead of a misleading p99.
Sam: UX ask: show a small badge on p99 when mixed-origin exists: "mixed-origin — see breakdown". That avoids customers misinterpreting numbers.
Lina: Quick patch idea: keep current p99 behavior but add an opt-in query param: ?provenance=true that returns the origin breakdown. That keeps payload small by default.
Raj: But the console wants badge by default. We could have console set provenance=true for rollup queries only (since console is heavy). Server must ensure this path is rate-limited.
Eve: Concern: computing per-origin t-digests on large cardinality (tenant+route+origin) could be expensive. Alternative: maintain origin counts and only compute per-origin t-digests for top N origins at query time. For others aggregate into 'other' and compute a coarse quantile via reservoir samples.
Lina: low-effort mitigation: if rollup detects tiny untagged tail (count < 1% total but value >> route p99) show "outlier origin present" and include a trace link to raw logs.
Raj: Technical API sketch (proto-style but inline):
```
GET /telemetry/rollup?route=/v1/generate&window=30m&provenance=true
Response: {
  p50: 120,
  p95: 420,
  p99: 890,
  sample_count: 230,
  provenance: { "top_origins": [{"name":"variant-a","count":120,"p99":210},{"name":"variant-b","count":110,"p99":700}], "other_count":0, "mixed_origin": true }
}
```
Sam: That looks good. Product note: please include a human-friendly explanation when mixed_origin is true, something like "Percentiles computed across multiple origin labels (e.g., variant, route). View breakdown to see which origin contributes to tail."
Eve: Devops: let's also add a small alert when rollup mixed_origin persists >5m with p99 > 2*slo. That'll catch real regressions.
Raj: Implementation plan: I can prototype server-side changes to include top-origin counts and p99s using existing per-shard summaries. Will add a flag to disable heavy computations for low-tier users.
Lina: Timeline?
Raj: I'll open a PR tomorrow with the API + a flag. Estimate 2 days to get a prototype, 1 day for console changes to add badge + explore pane.
Sam: Product OK with that timeline. Keep me posted. If you need a UX mock I can throw one together.
Lina: Thanks all — good to know this was a telemetry artifact and we have a mitigations path. :thumbsup:
telemetry-bot: NOTE: created ticket T-4551 "rollup provenance metadata + mixed-origin badge" assigned to Raj.
Raj: I'll reference this thread in the PR.
Eve: Follow-up: we should also scan for other recent deploys that toggled optional attributes (search deploy log between 1735218000 and 1735220000).
